src/application/OrderService.ts: constructor(orders: OrderRepository, products: ProductRepository); every public method returns OrderDto via private toDto(order: Order)
src/application/OrderService.ts: domain rules are delegated, not duplicated: product.reserve(item.quantity), product.release(line.quantity), order.advanceTo(status), order.cancel()
src/application/OrderDtos.ts: shared contracts CreateProductInput, CreateOrderInput, OrderDto, ProductDto are used by both services

parsedVerdict.reasoning: The src/application module is one cohesive concern: the application layer of an ordering system. CatalogueService and OrderService follow the same pattern. Both take domain repository interfaces through the constructor, throw DomainError for failures and return DTOs defined in OrderDtos.ts through a private toDto mapper. Each toDto covers a different entity (Product vs Order), so neither duplicates the other. State-changing rules are delegated to domain objects (Product.reserve/release, Order.advanceTo/cancel) rather than reimplemented. Neither service bypasses the repositories. Minor issues, none serious enough to fail: (1) OrderService has a getOrder helper for the order-not-found check but writes the product-not-found check out twice (placeOrder and cancelOrder). This is local repetition in one file, not a rule split across files. (2) OrderDtos.ts also holds product DTOs (ProductDto, CreateProductInput), so its name is narrower than what it contains. (3) The {productId, quantity} item shape is written inline in several places instead of as a named type. None of these splits the module into unrelated concerns or splits an invariant across files.
